results.title: Soundness of first-order natural deduction
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\Gamma$ be a finite list of formulas of a first-order language $L$ with free variables in $\alpha$, and let $\varphi$ be such a formula. If $\Gamma \vdash \varphi$ in natural deduction, then for every $L$-structure $M$ and every assignment $v \colon \alpha \to M$ under which all members of $\Gamma$ hold, $\varphi$ holds under $v$.

results.title: Weakening
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\alpha$ be an infinite type of variables, let $\Gamma$ and $\Delta$ be finite lists of formulas of a first-order language $L$ with free variables in $\alpha$ such that every member of $\Gamma$ is a member of $\Delta$, and let $\varphi$ be such a formula. If $\Gamma \vdash \varphi$ in natural deduction, then $\Delta \vdash \varphi$.

results.title: Cut
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\Gamma$ be a finite list of formulas of a first-order language $L$ with free variables in $\alpha$, let $\varphi$ and $\psi$ be such formulas, and write $\varphi, \Gamma$ for the list $\Gamma$ with $\varphi$ added in front. If $\Gamma \vdash \varphi$ and $\varphi, \Gamma \vdash \psi$ in natural deduction, then $\Gamma \vdash \psi$.

results.title: Symmetry of equality in natural deduction
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\Gamma$ be a list of first-order formulas and let $s$ and $t$ be terms. If the equation $s = t$ is derivable from the hypotheses $\Gamma$, then the equation $t = s$ is derivable from $\Gamma$.

results.title: Transitivity of equality in natural deduction
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\Gamma$ be a list of first-order formulas and let $r$, $s$ and $t$ be terms. If the equations $r = s$ and $s = t$ are both derivable from the hypotheses $\Gamma$, then the equation $r = t$ is derivable from $\Gamma$.

results.title: Provability from a set of formulas
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A set $T$ of formulas of a first-order language $L$ with free variables in $\alpha$ proves such a formula $\varphi$ when there is a finite list $\Gamma$ of members of $T$ with $\Gamma \vdash \varphi$ in natural deduction.

results.title: Soundness for theories
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $T$ be a theory, that is, a set of sentences of a first-order language $L$, and regard each sentence of $T$ as a formula with free variables in $\alpha$. If a formula $\varphi$ with free variables in $\alpha$ is provable from these formulas, then $\varphi$ holds in every model of $T$ under every assignment of elements of the model to the variables in $\alpha$.

results.title: Primes in the upper Oppermann interval
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a natural number $n$, this is the number of primes $p$ with $n^2 \le p \le n^2 + n$.

results.title: Main term for the Oppermann prime counts
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a natural number $n$, this is the real number $n / (2 \log n)$, where $\log$ is the natural logarithm. It is used as the asymptotic main term for the number of primes in each of the intervals $[n^2 - n, n^2]$ and $[n^2, n^2 + n]$.

results.title: Robin's criterion for the Riemann hypothesis
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The Riemann hypothesis holds if and only if $\sigma(n) < e^{\gamma}\, n \log\log n$ for every natural number $n > 5040$, where $\sigma(n)$ is the sum of the positive divisors of $n$, $\gamma$ is the Euler–Mascheroni constant, and $\log$ is the natural logarithm.

results.title: Robin exceptional set
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a real number $x$, the Robin exceptional set up to $x$ is the set of natural numbers $n$ with $7! = 5040 < n \le x$ that fail Robin's inequality, that is, with $\sigma(n) \ge e^\gamma n \log\log n$, where $\sigma(n)$ is the sum of the divisors of $n$ and $\gamma$ is the Euler–Mascheroni constant. Its cardinality is the counting function $N_R(x)$.

results.title: The Robin exceptional set is empty up to $7!$
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every real $x \le 7! = 5040$, the Robin exceptional set up to $x$ is empty; that is, its cardinality $N_R(x)$ is $0$.

results.title: Lucas derivative
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For real numbers $\varphi$ and $\varphi'$, the Lucas derivative $D_{\varphi,\varphi'}$ sends a function $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ to the function whose value at $x \ne 0$ is $(f(\varphi x) - f(\varphi' x))/((\varphi - \varphi')x)$, read as $0$ when $\varphi = \varphi'$, and whose value at $0$ is the derivative $f'(0)$, read as $0$ when $f$ is not differentiable at $0$.

results.title: The Lucas derivative away from the origin
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For all real numbers $\varphi$, $\varphi'$ and $x \ne 0$ and every function $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$, the Lucas derivative $D_{\varphi,\varphi'}$ satisfies $D_{\varphi,\varphi'} f(x) = (f(\varphi x) - f(\varphi' x))/((\varphi - \varphi')x)$, where the quotient is read as $0$ when $\varphi = \varphi'$.

results.title: The Lucas derivative at the origin
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For all real numbers $\varphi$, $\varphi'$ and every function $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$, the Lucas derivative $D_{\varphi,\varphi'}$ satisfies $D_{\varphi,\varphi'} f(0) = f'(0)$, where $f'(0)$ is read as $0$ when $f$ is not differentiable at $0$.

results.title: The Lucas derivative of the identity

results.title: Eneström–Kakeya theorem
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $n \ge 1$ and let $a_0, a_1, \dots, a_n$ be positive real numbers. Then every complex zero $z$ of the polynomial $f(z) = a_0 + a_1 z + \dots + a_n z^n$ satisfies $\rho_1 \le |z| \le \rho_2$, where $\rho_1$ and $\rho_2$ are the minimum and the maximum of the ratios $a_k / a_{k+1}$ for $0 \le k \le n - 1$.

results.title: Jentzsch's theorem
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $(a_k)_{k \ge 0}$ be complex numbers such that the power series $\sum_{k \ge 0} a_k z^k$ has radius of convergence $1$, and for $n \ge 0$ let $s_n(z) = \sum_{k=0}^{n} a_k z^k$ be its $n$-th partial sum. Then for every complex $z$ with $|z| = 1$, every real $\varepsilon > 0$ and every natural number $N$, there are $n \ge N$ and a root $w$ of the polynomial $s_n$ with $|w - z| < \varepsilon$.

This is the deterministic automaton over $T \sqcup T$ with the two states true and false, whose start state and only accepting state are true, and which moves from state $b$ on a letter $c$ to true exactly when $b$ is true and $c$ lies in the left copy, and to false otherwise.

results.title: Automaton running a deterministic automaton on the right copy
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $D$ be a deterministic automaton over an alphabet $T$, and write $T \sqcup T$ for the disjoint union of a left and a right copy of $T$. This is the deterministic automaton over $T \sqcup T$ whose states are the states of $D$ together with one extra dead state $\bot$. results.title: Forgetting the copy of a letter
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For an alphabet $T$, write $T \sqcup T$ for the disjoint union of a left and a right copy of $T$. This map sends the left copy and the right copy of a letter $a \in T$ to the one-letter word $a$ over $T$.

results.title: Satisfiability of a closed linear μ-calculus formula
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A closed linear μ-calculus formula is satisfiable: some word and position satisfy it under the empty environment.

results.title: Validity of a closed linear μ-calculus formula
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A closed linear μ-calculus formula is valid: every word and position satisfy it under the empty environment.

results.title: Linear μ-calculus model checking on a finite Kripke structure
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Model checking a linear μ-calculus formula against a finite Kripke structure: every infinite path `π` from `start` following `edges` satisfies `φ` at position `0`, where the path turns the structure's valuation `worldVal` into a word valuation.

results.title: Linear μ-calculus satisfiability as a decision problem
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Satisfiability of the linear μ-calculus as a decision problem over bitstrings: the input decodes to a formula token list, which decodes to a formula; the answer is whether that formula is closed and satisfiable.

results.title: Linear μ-calculus model checking as a decision problem
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Model checking of the linear μ-calculus as a decision problem over bitstrings: the input decodes to `(n, edges, worldVals, start, tokens)`, where `worldVals` lists, per world, the atoms true at that world; the answer is whether the decoded formula is closed, the structure is well-formed and total (every world has a successor world, so the path quantification is not vacuous at deadlocks), and every path from `start`…
